title: Add global editor add-on loader
body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/831

Implement the first part of my [global plugin proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/831#issuecomment-3355144722), which added a new global/editor resource file directory that can be accessed from all projects.

By the way, this PR appears to also solve the fourth point of the proposal, which is making the global resources editable.

## Goal:
The goal of this PR is to make the minimum required system for external resources (for editor plugins) to be load into the editor, just enough feature for it function without errors/bugs. This is so that the review process will not be too overwhelming. Missing features will need to be addressed in follow-up PRs.

The general idea of this PR is that you can place resources/addons into the editor resource folder located in the editor data folder, and it will be loaded into the editor like normal project resources.

## Feature:
- An external resource directory to place the global/editor resources. (Located in the Godot data folder: `%APPDATA%/Godot/editor_resources/4.6/`)
- Global resource files (such as resources, custom classes, and add-ons) load into the editor like normal project resources.
- ~~Global resource files also load into the **running project** if launched from the editor.~~
- You can access the global directory using the `editor://` path prefix.
- The resources are editable by the editor. (That is, if you managed to get access to them, e.g., a script or exports from a custom node.)
- In an exported project, the `editor://` path should not work. (I didn't test yet.)

## Usage:
- Launch the editor to generate the global directory folder.
- Then go to the Godot data folder (you can easily find it in your project under `editor->open editor data/settings folder`)
- Once in the data folder, navigate to `editor_resources/4.6/` and place your resources/addons there.
- The resources will load into the editor on all projects. They will behave like your typical project resources.
> [!NOTE]  
> Some addons will not work out of the box, because they were referencing resources that is meant to be in `res://`. So some modification to the addon is needed.
>
> You could use my [follow up PR,](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114823) which added the `editor://` files into the editor filesystem dock and allowed resources editing and saving, for easier modifications.

## Tested environment

### Operating system:
- Windows 11. Tested by (me) @PiCode9560
- Linux. Tested by @rsubtil https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111193#issuecomment-3728799690
- MacOS 15.7.2. Tested by @MartinDelille https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111193#issuecomment-3769193986
 
### Addons:
Tested with these addons:
- [Inspector-Tabs](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/3951)
- [Script-IDE](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/2206)
- [godot-vim](https://github.com/wenqiangwang/godot-vim)
- [Godot-Quick-Scenes](https://github.com/KoBeWi/Godot-Quick-Scenes)
- [Edit Resources as Table 2](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/1479)
- [DualEditor](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/3563)
- [Ridiculous Coding](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/1559)

> [!NOTE]
> Some of these addons need to update their path reference from `res:// to `editor:// for them to work.

## Roadmap

Follow-up features that (might) need to be added:
- [make the global resources completely editor only.](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/831#issuecomment-3703682084)
- Move `editor://` plugins settings to `EditorSettings`: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117450
- Add the `editor://` directory to the filesystem dock: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114823
- [More suggestions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111193#pullrequestreview-3648290048) from @KoBeWi
